paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the proud one is not winning. It looks like he is. He's piling up loans, building his house up high, and putting up a whole city. But God says all that labor "only feeds the fire" (Habakkuk 2:13). When something is built on what isn't yours, it falls on the builder (Habakkuk 2:6-8).

Now look at what God does here. Habakkuk asked why God was silent while the wicked swallowed up people more righteous than themselves (Habakkuk 1:13). God answers by saying that the one who plunders will be plundered, and that the cup in His right hand "will come around" (Habakkuk 2:16). So when the wrong keeps going and you feel like asking "How long?", you can trust that God sees it. I asked that very question from the back of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, He had His eye on it the whole time.

The other thing God shows us is where to put our trust. An idol has gold and silver on it, but "there is no breath in it at all" (Habakkuk 2:19). The proud one's stuff can't give guidance either. But "the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth be silent before Him" (Habakkuk 2:20). So when you can't see the whole picture, baker, stop shouting at the wood and stone. Be still, because the earth will be filled "with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea" (Habakkuk 2:14).
